newsitem.title: UK: Russian police clash with Chechens - agency.
newsitem.headline: Russian police clash with Chechens - agency.

text.p: Russian police have clashed with a Chechen "gang" near the border with the separatist Chechnya region and there were casualties on both sides, Russia's Interfax news agency reported on Tuesday.

The agency, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, quoted the commander of Russian forces in the North Caucasus, Partagen Andriyevskiy, as saying the Chechens had crossed the border and were trying to make their way into the neigbouring region of Dagestan. He said there were dead and wounded on both sides.
All crossing points on the Chechen border were being closed from 0200 GMT on Tuesday, Andriyevskiy said. Troops all along the border were on full alert, he added.
A powerful explosion tore apart a railway station in southern Russia on Monday, killing at least one person and injuring 17 in the second suspected bomb blast in five days.

Russian officials said they suspected Chechen separatists were behind the evening explosion at the station in Pyatigorsk, about 130 km (80 miles) northwest of Chechnya. Chechen leaders denied the charges. Two people were killed in a bomb blast at Armavir railway station in southern Russia last Wednesday.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin said he was deeply concerned and made clear relations with the separatist leaders of Chechnya would deteriorate sharply if a Chechen link was confirmed and they did not crack down.
